queen-victoria-her-girlhood-and-womanhoo: Grace Greenwood — the pen name of pioneering journalist Sara Jane Lippincott — wrote this life of Queen Victoria for young readers. From a sheltered princess to the long-reigning empress of a global empire, Victoria's story unfolds with warmth and admiration. The biography shows how Victorian girls were taught to see their remarkable queen.
the-flood: Émile Zola's powerful short novel depicts a Provençal village destroyed by flood — nature's indifference crashing against human fragility. His naturalist's eye spares nothing in scenes of terror and loss. A devastating, beautifully written catastrophe from the master of realism.
the-good-news-of-god: Charles Kingsley preaches the good news of God — a gospel of joy, work, and love for common folk. His sermons ring with hope and manly tenderness. The beloved parson's faith at its most winning. Joy, honest work, and love for one's fellows ring through these hopeful, hearty sermons.
my-boyhood: John Burroughs recalls his boyhood on a New York farm — the woods, the chores, the birth of a naturalist. His gentle memoir shows where his love of nature began. A beautiful American autobiography. Trout streams, winter coasts, and first books shaped the coming naturalist.
the-leatherwood-god: William Dean Howells' stark novel tells of the Leatherwood God — the Ohio impostor who claimed divinity and met a grim end. Based on a true story, it is Howells' darkest and most powerful work. A chilling American tale. Joseph Dylks' strange career ended in a madhouse, but Howells found tragedy in it.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adam-blackwoo: A 1913 entry on Adam Blackwood — the Scots controversialist who defended Mary Stuart. Oswald Hunter-Blair honors his loyal pen. His Martyrdom of Mary answered the rebels. A scholar's sword for a captive queen. His Latin verses graced the royal cause. Exile in Poitiers never broke him.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-adulteration-: This 1913 reference piece on adulteration of food — the cheating of buyers with false goods. Thomas Sloane treats its moral side. Watered milk and sanded sugar wrong the poor. The Church condemns the fraud. Honest weights, honestly kept. Public analysts now guard the marketplace.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-anthony-of-th: A 1913 Catholic Encyclopedia entry on Anthony of the Mother of God — a religious of note. John Joseph A'Becket records his life. The entry preserves his modest fame. His order honors its devout sons. A name in the Church's annals. His feast graces the order's calendar.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-archconfrater: This 1913 reference article on the Archconfraternity of the Most Precious Blood — the devotion to Christ's blood. Ulrich Müller describes its pious work. Its members honor the redeeming stream. Rome's church is its center. A confraternity of the sacred price.
catholic-encyclopedia-1913-association-o: This 1913 reference piece on the Association of the Holy Childhood — the children's mission society. John Willms tells its worldwide work. A Hail Mary a day, a penny a month. The little ones ransom pagan babes. The Church's smallest missionaries. Its annals tell of millions saved.
